claims.text: Replacing traditional EAM reference potentials with a deep-neural-network ML potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The ML reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The target systems include both solid and liquid high-entropy alloys at approximately 0.9–1.1 Tm.
High-entropy-alloy liquids near melting exhibit vast atomic configurational diversity.
The proposed ML potential will be trained on an extensive ab initio dataset containing configurations from both solid and liquid phases.
The method is applicable to equimolar or near-equimolar high-entropy alloys near 0.9–1.1 Tm.
A deep-neural-network potential provides a high-dimensional representation of atomic interactions.
The ML potential will capture diverse local atomic environments better than EAM potentials.
Training across the relevant temperature and composition space will improve reproduction of the ab initio energy landscapes of both solid and liquid states.
Closer reproduction of the ab initio potential over the sampled configurations will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The intervention is expected to significantly narrow the free-energy discrepancy along the integration path.
TOR-TILD currently uses traditional EAM references.
TOR-TILD's EAM references have inadequate phase-space overlap with the ab initio liquid state.
Insufficient sampling of liquid configurational space during training may prevent the ML potential from improving the calculation.
Failure to generalize to unseen atomic configurations may prevent the ML potential from improving the calculation.
The method's effectiveness is expected to be limited to high-entropy-alloy compositions and temperatures near melting.
The proposed benchmark compares ML-reference and EAM-reference thermodynamic-integration calculations against the same ab initio target over temperatures near Tm.
The hypothesis is falsified if the ML reference produces no statistically significant reduction in path mismatch, or produces a worse mismatch, relative to the EAM reference.
